claims.text: Periodic Bloom filter transmission can impose high overhead in communication-constrained distributed systems.
claims.poster_quote: Periodic Bloom filter transmission can impose high overhead in communication-constrained distributed systems.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Periodic Bloom-filter transmission can impose substantial overhead in communication-constrained distributed systems.
claims.reason: Abstract, first sentence: The paper explicitly states that periodic Bloom-filter transmission can impose substantial overhead in communication-constrained distributed systems.

claims.text: Lossless compression preserves membership but yields only one size.
claims.poster_quote: Lossless compression preserves membership but yields only one size.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Lossless compression preserves membership behavior but provides a single transmission size.
claims.reason: Abstract, second sentence: The paper states that lossless compression preserves membership behavior but provides a single transmission size.

claims.text: OR folding creates smaller, queryable views with higher FPR while preserving no-false-negative property.
claims.poster_quote: OR folding creates smaller, queryable views with higher FPR while preserving no-false-negative property.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: OR folding produces smaller representations with higher false-positive rates (FPRs) while preserving the no-false-negative property.
claims.reason: Abstract, third sentence: The paper explicitly states that OR folding produces smaller representations with higher FPRs while preserving the no-false-negative property.

claims.text: Sender retains canonical filter, constructs FPR-qualified catalog, and selects largest supported view per reporting opportunity.
claims.poster_quote: sender retains canonical filter, constructs FPR-qualified catalog, and selects largest supported view per reporting opportunity.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The sender retains an unchanged canonical filter, constructs a catalog satisfying a maximum FPR, and selects the FPR-qualified representation with the largest retained length supported by the communication resources available at each reporting opportunity.
claims.reason: Abstract, fourth sentence: The paper describes the sender retaining the canonical filter, constructing a catalog, and selecting the largest FPR-qualified representation supported by communication resources.

claims.text: Goal: improve communication efficiency and receiver freshness under time-varying channels, while preserving no-false-negative property.
claims.poster_quote: Goal: improve communication efficiency and receiver freshness under time-varying channels, while preserving no-false-negative property.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The research objective is to determine whether channel-aware selection among FPR-qualified folded views improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness relative to fixed complete-filter and lossless-compression baselines while preserving the no-false-negative property.
claims.reason: Introduction, paragraph 6: The paper explicitly states the goal of improving communication efficiency and receiver freshness under time-varying channels while preserving the no-false-negative property.

claims.text: Baselines include complete canonical filter, sparse canonical filter, and four lossless compression methods (gzip, zlib, bzip2, LZMA) at highest compression level.
claims.poster_quote: Baselines: complete canonical filter, sparse canonical filter, and four lossless compression methods (gzip, zlib, bzip2, LZMA) at highest compression level.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Evaluation uses two phishing URL datasets and Five-State Markov Capacity, Gilbert–Elliott burst-error, and Rayleigh block-fading models.
claims.reason: Abstract, sixth sentence: The paper mentions the evaluation includes two phishing URL datasets and three channel models. Section IV.C lists the four lossless compression methods used as baselines.

claims.text: Metrics include communication efficiency (successful deliveries per MB of attempted wire bytes), receiver freshness (mean number of intervals since last successful update), and FPR (empirical false positive rate per retained-length ratio).
claims.poster_quote: Metrics: (1) Communication efficiency: successful deliveries per MB of attempted wire bytes. (2) Receiver freshness: mean number of intervals since last successful update. (3) FPR: empirical false positive rate per retained-length ratio.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Communication efficiency is measured as successful report deliveries per one million attempted wire bytes. Receiver age is the number of transmission-opportunity intervals since the most recent successful delivery. Bloom-filter performance is measured by empirical FPR versus retained-length ratio.
claims.reason: Section IV.F: The paper explicitly defines communication efficiency, receiver freshness, and FPR as evaluation metrics.

claims.text: All strategies use the same channel trace per repetition.
claims.poster_quote: All strategies use same channel trace per repetition.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Within each dataset, model, and repetition, all strategies use the same channel trace.
claims.reason: Section IV.A: The paper states that all strategies use the same channel trace within each dataset, model, and repetition.

claims.text: Datasets include PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish, with 5,000 malicious URLs inserted and 50,000 benign queries.
claims.poster_quote: Datasets: PhiUSIIL and URL-Phish, 5,000 malicious URLs inserted, 50,000 benign queries.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The PhiUSIIL [14] and URL-Phish [15] datasets are evaluated using 5,000 malicious URLs for insertion and 50,000 disjoint benign URLs as absent queries.
claims.reason: Section IV.A: The paper explicitly describes the datasets and the number of malicious and benign URLs used.

claims.text: Sender retains canonical Bloom filter and generates catalog of OR-folded views at various retained-length ratios (e.g., 0.95m, 0.90m, 0.75m).
claims.poster_quote: Sender retains canonical Bloom filter and generates catalog of OR-folded views at various retained-length ratios (e.g., 0.95m, 0.90m, 0.75m).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The catalog includes the complete canonical representation and progressively smaller OR-folded representations.
claims.reason: Section III.E: The paper describes the sender generating a catalog of OR-folded views at various retained-length ratios.

claims.text: Each view is associated with its measured FPR.
claims.poster_quote: Each view is associated with its measured FPR.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Each candidate is associated with its retained length and measured FPR, and representations exceeding the application-defined maximum FPR are excluded.
claims.reason: Section III.E: The paper explicitly states that each view is associated with its measured FPR.

claims.text: At each reporting opportunity, sender selects the largest FPR-qualified view that fits current communication constraints (capacity or loss probability).
claims.poster_quote: At each reporting opportunity, sender selects the largest FPR-qualified view that fits current communication constraints (capacity or loss probability).
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: At each reporting opportunity, the sender obtains an estimate of the current communication conditions from the underlying communication system and selects the highest-fidelity FPR-qualified representation supported under those conditions.
claims.reason: Section III.E: The paper describes the sender selecting the largest FPR-qualified view that fits current communication constraints.

claims.text: Transmitted update includes view, its length, and timestamp.
claims.poster_quote: Transmitted update includes view, its length, and timestamp.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: Each transmitted update contains the selected Bloom-filter representation, its retained length m′ , and a timestamp that serves as its report version.
claims.reason: Section III.E: The paper explicitly states that transmitted updates include the view, its length, and a timestamp.

claims.text: Receiver installs only newer, fully delivered updates and queries using two-stage coordinate mapping.
claims.poster_quote: Receiver installs only newer, fully delivered updates and queries using two-stage coordinate mapping.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The receiver installs only a completely delivered update newer than its currently stored view and queries it using the coordinate mapping in Equation (5).
claims.reason: Section III.E: The paper describes the receiver installing only newer, fully delivered updates and using a two-stage coordinate mapping for queries.

claims.text: Experiments fix inserted set, canonical length, and hash count to isolate channel effects.
claims.poster_quote: Experiments fix inserted set, canonical length, and hash count to isolate channel effects.
claims.label: supported
claims.paper_evidence: The experiments hold the inserted set, canonical filter length, hash count, and candidate catalog constant.
claims.reason: Section III.E: The paper explicitly states that the experiments fix the inserted set, canonical length, and hash count to isolate channel effects.

claims.text: Under Five-State Markov: adaptive folding achieves 191.6 deliveries/MB vs. 66.9 (best compression) and 27.7 (classical filter) — 2.9x and 6.9x improvement.
claims.poster_quote: Under Five-State Markov: adaptive folding achieves 191.6 deliveries/MB vs. 66.9 (best compression) and 27.7 (classical filter) — 2.9x and 6.9x improvement.

claims.text: Under Gilbert-Elliott: folding (140.5) and best compression (141.8) are comparable, classical filter (119.0) lags.
claims.poster_quote: Under Gilbert-Elliott: folding (140.5) and best compression (141.8) are comparable, classical filter (119.0) lags.

claims.text: Under Rayleigh: folding (174.9) vs. compression (89.9) and classical (58.2) — 1.9x and 3.0x improvement.
claims.poster_quote: Under Rayleigh: folding (174.9) vs. compression (89.9) and classical (58.2) — 1.9x and 3.0x improvement.

claims.text: Mean selected FPRs: 4.36% (Five-State), 3.43% (Gilbert-Elliott), 3.34% (Rayleigh), all ≤10% with zero false negatives.
claims.poster_quote: Mean selected FPRs: 4.36% (Five-State), 3.43% (Gilbert-Elliott), 3.34% (Rayleigh), all ≤10% with zero false negatives.

claims.text: Under Five-State Markov: folding reduces mean receiver age to 1.24 intervals vs. 13.5 (compression) and 31.6 (classical) — 10.9x and 25.5x fresher.
claims.poster_quote: Under Five-State Markov: folding reduces mean receiver age to 1.24 intervals vs. 13.5 (compression) and 31.6 (classical) — 10.9x and 25.5x fresher.

claims.text: Under Gilbert-Elliott: folding (0.31) is freshest vs. compression (0.39) and classical (0.49).
claims.poster_quote: Under Gilbert-Elliott: folding (0.31) is freshest vs. compression (0.39) and classical (0.49).

claims.text: Under Rayleigh: folding (0.40) vs. compression (1.02) and classical (1.72) — 61% and 77% fresher.
claims.poster_quote: Under Rayleigh: folding (0.40) vs. compression (1.02) and classical (1.72) — 61% and 77% fresher.

claims.text: Folding consistently delivers fresher state by selecting smaller views when channel conditions constrain transmission, preventing deferral.
claims.poster_quote: Folding consistently delivers fresher state by selecting smaller views when channel conditions constrain transmission, preventing deferral.

claims.text: OR-based folding maps canonical positions to folded space via modulo arithmetic: b’[i] = OR of all b[j] where j mod m’ = i.
claims.poster_quote: OR-based folding maps canonical positions to folded space via modulo arithmetic: b’[i] = OR of all b[j] where j mod m’ = i.

claims.text: For non-integer ratios, membership query uses two-stage mapping: H_i(x) mod m (canonical), then mod m’ (folded).
claims.poster_quote: For non-integer ratios, membership query uses two-stage mapping: H_i(x) mod m (canonical), then mod m’ (folded).

claims.text: This preserves no-false-negative property.
claims.poster_quote: This preserves no-false-negative property.

claims.text: FPR increases as retained ratio r = m’/m decreases, due to merging of canonical positions.
claims.poster_quote: FPR increases as retained ratio r = m’/m decreases, due to merging of canonical positions.

claims.text: Empirical FPR is measured per candidate; only views with FPR ≤ 10% are eligible for selection.
claims.poster_quote: Empirical FPR is measured per candidate; only views with FPR ≤ 10% are eligible for selection.

claims.text: Channel-aware selection of OR-folded Bloom filters improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness under time-varying channels, especially when opportunities vary substantially (Five-State, Rayleigh).
claims.poster_quote: Channel-aware selection of OR-folded Bloom filters improves communication efficiency and receiver freshness under time-varying channels, especially when opportunities vary substantially (Five-State, Rayleigh).

claims.text: Under favorable conditions (Gilbert-Elliott), it remains competitive in efficiency and provides the freshest receiver state.
claims.poster_quote: Under favorable conditions (Gilbert-Elliott), it remains competitive in efficiency and provides the freshest receiver state.

claims.text: Smaller views trade higher FPR for fresher updates, preserving no-false-negative property.
claims.poster_quote: Smaller views trade higher FPR for fresher updates, preserving no-false-negative property.

claims.text: This approach is useful when recent, lower-fidelity updates are preferable to delayed, larger ones.
claims.poster_quote: This approach is useful when recent, lower-fidelity updates are preferable to delayed, larger ones.

claims.text: Future work should address fixed-folded baselines, dynamic contents, and real-world channel conditions.
claims.poster_quote: Future work should address fixed-folded baselines, dynamic contents, and real-world channel conditions.
